assertion.statement: For the retained common family and its integral identity f_x*u_x=d_x, the finite coefficient argument produces a nonzero address x with v2(u_x(0)-u_0(0))>=M-2c>B. The base-zero implication then contradicts the nonzero-address upper bound and gives analytic order1 for E.
assertion.objects: The same corrected class-functional coordinates u_x, elements f,d in O[G], O=completion of Z2[[t]] localized at(2), and binary addresses x in F2^b.
assertion.hypotheses: The previous common-denominator construction supplies f0 in Lambda, c=v2 f0(0)<=c_det, an all-negative-tail cutoff L_T(M), regular u_x and u_0 in Lambda[1/2], and integral d. A fixed B bounds nonzero-address central valuations before b is chosen. The base derivative-zero implication and nonzero complementary L-value are separate inputs. Also retain L(E,1)=0, obtained from the root number -1 supplied by rational full-corank parity and the functional equation. The complementary central value is nonzero.
assertion.quantifiers: Choose an integer M>max(c_det,B+2c_det), then b>(L_T(M)+2)(2^M-1), before the graph and theta precision. A nonzero binary address satisfying all listed congruences exists.
assertion.parameter_range: Coefficients in the original group basis; t-Laurent coefficients are Z2-valued. Test coefficients of f from -L_T(M) through0 and the constant coefficient of d.
assertion.uniformity: c_det,B and L_T depend on the previously fixed K and data, not on b or the subsequently realized graph.
assertion.constants: Bit j has Boolean degree at most2^(j-1). The resulting error bound is M-c and the central-coordinate difference bound is M-2c>B.
assertion.normalizations: Use the same integral determinant basis and corrected coordinate throughout. Original group-ring coefficients, not separately interpolated sign values, give the Boolean polynomial constraints.
assertion.exceptional_cases: Every negative Laurent coefficient contributes to the convolution; the untested tail is controlled by the separate pole bound. No nonzero-address outer estimate is applied to the unknown base. Instead integrality of d0=f0*u0 gives v2 u0(0)>=-c.
assertion.limit_order: Fix K and all bounds, choose M and b, then realize the graph/theta stage. Use regularity to exclude negative powers of u before subtracting the full convergent constant-term convolution.
